Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

dialogue noun

also dialog, dialogues, talks (between two sides), hold talks, a written dialogue

classical

Caes. BG 1.35, 1.43: ad colloquium vēnērunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Phil. 12.26

colloquium, colloquiī n.

noun, second declension

a conversation, a meeting for talks

A talk between two people, and above all a meeting between two sides to talk things over: in colloquium venīre, to come to talks. Varro defines it as people meeting in one place to talk (LL 6.57).

Other words

  • sermō, sermōnis m. — a conversation, a talk

    noun, third declension · also used · classical

    The ordinary word for conversation (see talk); also the dialogue of a play or of Cicero’s philosophical works, which he calls sermōnēs.

  • dialogus, dialogī m. — a (written, philosophical) dialogue

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 44 fin.; Brut. 60 fin.; Quint. 5.14.27 (Lewis & Short)

    A Greek word, used by Cicero and Quintilian of the literary form, a dialogue like Plato’s; not of everyday talks between people.

Examples

  • in Antōniī congressum colloquiumque veniendum est

    we have to come to a meeting and talks with AntonyCic. Phil. 12.26 (Lewis & Short)

See also talk, negotiate, negotiation.
